messages.text: Tuesday, November 10 · Canton, Michigan
A quiet Tuesday drift beneath gray skies and the hum of distant neutrinos

The air remains unseasonably mild as we settle into a stretch of overcast November days. Locally, the conversation centers on new investments for our neighbors in need, while science looks toward the deep mysteries of our galaxy.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 64 degrees and a low around 40 degrees.
The sun rises at 7:19 AM and sets at 5:17 PM, with a new moon that is 1.1 percent illuminated.
A thoughtful evening in Ann Arbor

Consider the free film screening In the Belly of AI at the Ann Arbor District Library at 6:00 PM to explore the hidden costs of technology. Alternatively, the Veterans for Peace Concert at The Ark begins at 7:30 PM.
The 862 Meeting is scheduled for tomorrow, November 11, at 6:30 PM.
Supporting our community's warming centers

KeyBank Foundation has committed a 250,000 dollar investment to expand the Shelter Association of Washtenaw County's warming center and resource hub in Ypsilanti. This funding aims to support daily operations and food costs for approximately 40 people.
Looking toward the week ahead
Mark your calendar for the United Way Make a Difference Day on November 14 starting at 9:00 AM.

Wednesday, November 11 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast skies and the quiet rhythm of a Canton Tuesday
The day brings a steady, gray overcast with a gentle high near 60 degrees. Local attention turns toward community engagement and the persistent challenge of housing affordability in the region.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 60 degrees, a low of 34 degrees, and a 62 percent chance of precipitation.
The sun rises at 7:20 AM and sets at 5:16 PM, with a new moon that is 3.8 percent illuminated.
Crafts and conversation
The Michigan Union in Ann Arbor hosts Cookies, Crafts, & Climate at 4 PM, offering a space to make climate-themed bracelets and discuss environmental issues.
A meeting is scheduled for 6:30 PM this evening.
The local housing landscape

Ann Arbor is working to address housing costs that have risen nearly 50 percent since 2016. The city's Comprehensive Land Use Plan, approved in March 2026, seeks to mitigate these pressures by adjusting zoning in previously single-family areas.
Looking toward the end of the week
United Way's Make a Difference Day is set for the morning of November 14.
